science.headline:
How GLP-1
Treatments Work
science.body: GLP-1 medications mimic a natural hormone that signals fullness to the brain and slows stomach emptying, which can reduce appetite. They are used together with nutrition and physical activity. Some GLP-1 medications are FDA-approved brand-name products, and others are compounded and not FDA-approved. Results vary.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor's prescription for GLP-1 treatments?
faqs.answer: Yes. All GLP-1 treatments are prescription medications. You will consult with our licensed medical doctor or healthcare provider who evaluates your health history to determine candidacy and prescribe the right plan for you.

faqs.question: How do GLP-1 weight loss treatments work?
faqs.answer: GLP-1 medications mimic a natural hormone involved in appetite and digestion. This can reduce appetite and slow stomach emptying, so some patients feel full sooner and eat less. Results vary.

faqs.question: Will I lose muscle while losing weight?
faqs.answer: Weight loss can include loss of lean mass as well as fat. Your provider may recommend protein targets and strength activity to help support muscle, but outcomes vary.

faqs.question: How do I get started?
faqs.answer: Simply call our clinic or book an appointment online! You will talk with a licensed doctor who will review your health, answer your questions, and start your custom plan.

faqs.question: What is the difference between semaglutide and tirzepatide?
faqs.answer: Both medications mimic gut hormones that help control appetite and blood sugar. Semaglutide acts on the GLP-1 receptor. Tirzepatide acts on both the GLP-1 and GIP receptors. Your provider chooses between them based on your health history, your goals and how you respond, and neither is right for everyone.

faqs.question: Are compounded GLP-1 medications FDA-approved?
faqs.answer: No. Compounded medications are prepared by a licensed pharmacy for an individual patient and are not FDA-approved. FDA-approved versions are sold under brand names. Your provider will explain which options are available to you and how they differ in sourcing and cost.

faqs.question: Who qualifies for medical weight loss?
faqs.answer: Eligibility is a clinical decision. FDA-approved weight-management labeling for these medications generally covers adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher, or 27 or higher with a weight-related condition such as high blood pressure or type 2 diabetes. Your provider reviews your history, medications and labs before recommending any plan.
